reasons: Over-flagging: the existing Section 10(a) is a genuine Vendor-side indemnity covering 'all third-party allegations, claims, actions ... arising out of or in connection with (i) the Services; (ii) the Auction Platform', which on its face captures a third-party allegation that the Services or Platform infringe IP. Combined with the express non-infringement warranty at p0033 and the warranty-breach limb (iv), the clause does not 'exclude IP infringement' — the trigger under the guidance for a deviation.

On the playbook's classification semantics the clause meets (indeed exceeds) the fallback (Vendor IP indemnity, no cap needed because indemnification is carved out of the damages exclusion and uncapped) and materially the preferred position: the finding's own rationale confirms defence obligation, breach-of-law, data-incident, gross negligence/wilful misconduct coverage, standard procedure (p0053-p0055), and a suitably narrow Customer indemnity. The absence of an express standalone IP limb is a wording/mechanic refinement to be noted in the rationale, not redlined.

The redline is not actionable as rendered: the new text is appended after the full stop ending limb (v) with no '(vi)' label and no connecting 'or', leaving a dangling sentence fragment inside the enumerated list rather than the clean limb (vi) described in the rationale.

Correct disposition would be a 'compliant' finding noting that IP infringement is reached through the broad 'arising out of or in connection with the Services' limb plus the p0033 warranty, with the knowledge qualifier on the Creative limb flagged as a minor sub-element.
